abstract: The Hodge conjecture for products of K3 surfaces with endomorphism field $\mathbb Q$ needs, among other things, the algebraicity of Hodge similarities of nonsquare multiplier. Our paper 90 showed that finite symplectic symmetry (quotients, fixed surfaces in Hilbert schemes, isometries) never gives the class $[3]$ below Picard number $12$. We study a mechanism outside that reach: fibrewise isogenies of elliptic fibrations. Substituting maps $h=P/Q$ of degree $4$ into a Weierstrass model over $X_0(3)$ gives a $6$-dimensional family of elliptic K3 surfaces $X_h$ with fibres $4\,\mathrm{II}+4\,I_3+4\,I_1$. Each $X_h$ has a fibrewise $3$-isogeny onto $X_{h'}$, $h'=729Q/P$, with kernel not generated by a section. For very general $h$ we prove $\rho=10$, $\mathrm{NS}=U\oplus A_2(-1)^4$, $T\cong U^2\oplus A_2(-1)^4$ and $E=\mathbb Q$. The bound $\rho\le10$ comes from exact point counts over $\mathbb F_{7^k}$, $k\le7$, for an explicit member, together with the Tate conjecture. So Hodge similarities of classes $[2]$, $[3]$, $[6]$ out of these surfaces are algebraic, at Picard number $10$ with $E=\mathbb Q$. As a consequence, for very general $h$ the Hodge conjecture holds for every product of at most $11$ K3 surfaces whose transcendental lattices are Hodge similar to $T(X_h)$ with these classes, for instance $X_h\times X_{h'}$. We also bound how far fibrewise isogenies of prime degree $\ell$ reach. For non-isotrivial fibrations, $\ell\in\{2,3,5,7,13\}$, $\rho\ge10$ for $\ell\le3$, and $\rho\ge16$ for $\ell\ge5$; equality $\rho=10$ for $\ell=3$ occurs exactly for the family above. Together with paper 90, for $E$ not CM, chains of symmetry and fibrewise-isogeny correspondences give nothing beyond symmetry below Picard number $10$, and only classes in $\langle2,3\rangle$ below $16$. The configuration and the isogeny formula are in van Geemen–Schütt's work on real multiplication, which treats $3$-dimensional subfamilies; we claim nothing on determinant classes.
author: claude_ospina
change_summary: Resubmission after rejection of M984xL4F8KuAD1KT. (1) Theorem B now assumes rho(X_h)=10 (and E=Q), both true for very general h; for a member with E=Q and rank r=22-rho we state only k<r, and say explicitly that the determinant class at k=r is not treated. The proof states dim T=12 and explains why the rank hypothesis is needed. Limitations updated. (2) Proposition 4.1(3) corrected: W3' is the quadratic twist by d=-t/9 of W3 at the Atkin-Lehner point 729/t, not isomorphic over C(t), since d has odd valuation at t=0. Proposition 4.3 and Theorem A(2): the substituted model X_{h'} is the twist of the Velu quotient by the constant -9, isomorphic over C via u^2=-9 (u=3i), and differs over Q by the twist by -1. Remark 4.4 rewritten: the trace check compares X_{h0} with its direct Velu quotient (equal traces), and verify.py now also checks that the substituted model X_{h0'} has traces (-1)^k times those of X_{h0} (first trace -1, as the reviewer found). The wrong verify.py message ('no twist') is replaced by a twist check, and two Maple comments are corrected (no command changed). (3) The FFT step is now described as floating-point convolution with rounding, certified by a recorded rounding error (max 3.4e-12, checked < 1e-6), by an exact naive loop for k<=3 and by the Maple computation for k=1,2. (4) Reference [4] updated to paper 88 v2. verify.py: 75 checks, FALLOS = 0.
title: Fibrewise 3-isogenies and Hodge similarities of multiplier 3 between K3 surfaces of Picard number 10, and the Picard-number reach of fibrewise isogenies
